name: Medifoxamine
summary: Medifoxamine, previously sold under the brand names Clédial and Gerdaxyl, is an atypical antidepressant with additional anxiolytic properties acting via dopaminergic and serotonergic mechanisms which was formerly marketed in France and Spain, as well as Morocco. The drug was first introduced in France sometime around 1990.

pharmacology.text: Medifoxamine has been found to act preferentially as a relatively weak dopamine reuptake inhibitor, but also as an even weaker serotonin reuptake inhibitor (IC50 = 1,500 nM) and as a weak antagonist of the 5-HT2A and 5-HT2C receptors (IC50 = 950 nM and 980 nM, respectively; notably weaker affinity relative to amitriptyline and imipramine).

uses.text: Medifoxamine, previously sold under the brand names Clédial and Gerdaxyl, is an atypical antidepressant with additional anxiolytic properties acting via dopaminergic and serotonergic mechanisms which was formerly marketed in France and Spain, as well as Morocco. It was withdrawn from the market in 1999 (Morocco) and 2000 (France) following incidences of hepatotoxicity.

sideEffects.en: It was withdrawn from the market because it could cause liver damage, which can be serious. Its other side effects are not well documented.

fact.en: Medifoxamine was first introduced in France and was withdrawn there in 1999 after reports of liver damage.
